title: Mycobacterial Lipoarabinomannan: Rethinking Immunomodulation and Diagnosis of Tuberculosis
content: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (M.tb) is the etiological agent of tuberculosis (TB), which remains the second major cause of global mortality among infectious diseases. The tuberculosis burden is further complicated by drug resistance and HIV comorbidities, mainly affecting disproportionately low- and middle-income countries. M.tb cell wall is highly complex, versatile, involved in host pathogen crosstalk and plays central role in modulating host immune responses. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the immunogenic properties of M.tb Lipoarabinomannan (LAM). We describe LAM heterogeneity, associated receptors, signalling pathways, pathogenesis and evaluate the diagnostic application of lateral flow urine lipoarabinomannan assay (LF-LAM). M.tb LAM binds with host C-type lectin receptors, specifically the mannose receptor and DC-SIGN receptor to inhibit pro-inflammatory interleukin-12, and tumor necrosis factor-alpha and while stimulating the anti-inflammatory interleukin-10. Intracellularly, M.tb LAM disrupts phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase signalling, preventing phago-lysosomal fusion, decreases dendritic cell maturation and antigen presentation, which ultimately promotes in mycobacterial survival in host macrophages. Currently, WHO recommends the lateral flow LF-LAM assays (e.g., Alere LAM and FujiLAM) in specific clinical sub-populations, primarily people living with HIV. The LAM based higher investigational assays are in development to broaden the diagnostic yield, but a significant evidence gap remains regarding test accuracy, and the clinical utility. Other associated challenges should be addressed such as implementation feasibility in HIV negative individuals and broader patient populations across low- and middle-income countries.
